name: sol_defi_lending_3
description: Self-liquidation profit exploit in lending protocol liquidation logic
question: The source file in `source` implements a liquidation function that lets a borrower liquidate their own undercollateralized position and still receive the liquidation bonus, discounted collateral price, or other liquidator incentive without any check preventing msg.sender (or a controlled proxy) from being the position owner, allowing the user to extract undue profit or improperly close their own debt cheaply; this excludes designs where liquidation pays no bonus/discount, where self-liquidation is explicitly blocked or reverts, or where the liquidator incentive is capped so no net profit versus fair value is possible.
criteria: liquidate() transfers a liquidation bonus or discounted collateral to msg.sender without verifying msg.sender differs from the position owner being liquidated
the liquidation flow computes seized collateral using a discount factor applied uniformly even when the liquidator address equals the borrower address
a repay-and-seize function allows the borrower to call it on their own undercollateralized position and receive collateral at below-market price as the liquidation incentive
close factor logic permits full self-liquidation of an account's own debt while still granting the standard liquidation reward meant for third-party liquidators
